title: Maurya Empire
biography: The Maurya Empire was a geographically extensive Iron Age historical power based in Magadha and founded by Chandragupta Maurya. Under Ashoka the Great, the empire embraced Buddhism and spread its teachings across Asia, including to Sri Lanka through his son Mahinda.

sections.heading: Connection to Sri Lanka
content: Emperor Ashoka sent his son, Mahinda Thero, and later his daughter, Sanghamitta Theri, to Sri Lanka to introduce Buddhism.
This event fundamentally transformed Sri Lankan culture, architecture, and governance.

title: Ming Dynasty
biography: The Ming dynasty was the ruling dynasty of China from 1368 to 1644 following the collapse of the Mongol-led Yuan dynasty. It was the last imperial dynasty of China ruled by Han Chinese.

sections.heading: Connection to Sri Lanka
content: The Ming admiral Zheng He visited Sri Lanka multiple times during his treasure voyages in the 15th century.
The Galle Trilingual Inscription, erected by Zheng He, is a testament to the diplomatic and trade ties between the Ming court and the Kotte Kingdom.

title: Asuka & Nara Period
description: Introduction of Buddhism, centralization of the imperial state under Prince Shotoku, and construction of colossal bronze Buddhas at Todai-ji.

sections.heading: Key Developments

Establishment of the Seventeen-Article Constitution
Taiho Code legal system
First permanent imperial capital at Nara

title: Heian Period
description: Golden age of classical Japanese court culture, poetry, literature (Tale of Genji), and the rise of the warrior samurai clans.

title: Kamakura Shogunate
description: Establishment of Japan's first feudal military government under Shogun Minamoto no Yoritomo, repelling two Mongol invasions.

title: Old Kingdom of Egypt
